attempts.paper_title: Social isolation recruits amygdala–medial prefrontal cortex projections to escalate alcohol drinking in male mice (Nature Neuro)
attempts.entry_title: Social isolation and BLA-mPFC excitability and activity (Patel, Kim et al. 2026)
attempts.summary: Few of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data, and most that could did not hold up. Isolation's opposite effects on male and female drinking, and the optogenetic effects on drinking, are untestable because those behaviour data are not deposited. The fall in female BLA-mPFC excitability is untestable, as most isolated female recordings are empty, and the male rise failed with the neurons taken to be Figure 2's but passes with all deposited ones. Isolation and stimulation effects on mPFC alcohol and sucrose responses, and BLA-mPFC responses predicting drinking, did not reproduce on all imaged ROIs, as the curated neurons are not marked. Higher excitability in group-housed females and most controls held up.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Patel, Kim et al. (2026) that dandiset 001454 can test, which are the ex vivo current clamp recordings of BLA-mPFC and nonspecific BLA neurons (Figure 2, Extended Data Figs. 2 and 3) and the calcium imaging of BLA and mPFC neurons in the cued two-bottle choice, with and without BLA-mPFC terminal stimulation (Figures 3, 5 and 6). The home-cage drinking, rank, blood alcohol and optogenetic behaviour data are not in the dandiset, and the resident-intruder imaging has no interaction annotation.

outcomes.notes: With the 2022 cohort as the group-housed group (21 neurons from 7 mice) against 29 isolated neurons from 9 mice, the current by housing interaction is significant under both spike readings (F(25, 1200) = 4.70 and 4.83, p < 0.0001) and isolated neurons fire more at 14 of 26 steps (60 to 320 pA, up to 2.6 spikes at 180 pA) but fewer from 340 pA up (1.7 fewer at 500 pA). No step is significant after Sidak adjustment, with per-step t-tests (smallest adjusted p 0.116) or pooled error (0.325 and 0.346), so the Sidak part of the criterion fails and, with crossing curves, isolated neurons do not fire more across current injections. The variants of the spike rule give 14 or 15 of 26 steps and no Sidak step. With all 37 group-housed neurons the interaction holds, isolated neurons fire more at 17 of 26 steps, and per-step Sidak tests are significant at 120 to 180 pA, which would meet the criterion.

outcomes.notes: Against the 21 group-housed males (2022 cohort), the 16 recorded group-housed female neurons (8 mice) give a strong current by sex interaction (F(25, 875) = 17.84 and 19.37, p < 0.0001). Females fire more at 16 of 26 steps (0 mV) and 14 of 26 (-20 mV), and Sidak tests are significant at 80 to 200 pA and 80 to 180 pA (per step) where females fire more, so the criterion holds under both readings. Females fire significantly fewer spikes at the top currents (480 to 500 pA at 0 mV, 400 to 500 pA at -20 mV), so the higher excitability holds at low and middle currents. With the 5 mV re-arm variant females fire more at 12 of 26 steps with -20 mV, not most steps; without a re-arm, 17 and 16. With all 37 males, 19 and 14 of 26. The curves cross, as in fig2c, but the criterion asks for more firing at most steps and one significant Sidak step, and both hold; fig2c fails on its Sidak part, and its crossing is a further point against "across current injections". The -20 mV count still misses some female spikes (one mouse 2.08 spikes per step at -20 mV against 5.46 at 0 mV; 77 sweeps count fewer at -20 mV than at 0 mV), a bias against the claim.
deviations: 2 of the paper's 18 group-housed female neurons are in files without a recording; 16 are used.
Group-housed males are the 2022 cohort, as for fig2c (assumption; all 37 shown).

The paper used Clampfit. The 'most steps' part at -20 mV depends on this rule: the 5 mV re-arm gives 12 of 26.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds the current clamp recordings, the cued-2BC imaging sessions and the resident-intruder imaging sessions only. The home-cage 2BC licks, the tube-test ranks of the drinking and imaged mice, the blood alcohol values, the unimplanted control mice, the optogenetic behaviour sessions (ChR2, ChrimsonR, NpHR), the stability imaging of Extended Data Fig. 7 and the pose tracking and interaction annotation of the resident-intruder sessions are not in it, although the description lists pose tracking. 28 of the 61 claims cannot be tested for this reason.

13 of the 205 current clamp files hold no recording. Each holds a single voltage series and a single stimulus series named with the amplifier's secondary channel (VmSec, where every recorded file has VmPrime, ImPrime or ImPrime2), both flat (about 0.2, 0 or -209 mV, no step); their size, 31 or 62 MB, comes from histology images. They are 11 isolated female BLA-mPFC neurons (subjects M3.1, M3.3, M4.1, M4.2, M4.3, September 2024) and 2 group-housed ones (M2.2, August 2024), so only 3 isolated female neurons from one mouse remain. One isolated male file (M6.3, 2022-07-27) holds only the -120 pA sweep.

Three pairs of cued-2BC files hold identical fluorescence traces with different licks. Cohort16-M2-1 and Cohort16-M1-4, Cohort16-M3-4 and Cohort16-M3-3, and the isolation sucrose sessions of Cohort13b-M3-2 and Cohort13b-M2-2. In each pair the traces respond to the licks of the second file, so the first file carries another mouse's imaging.

All 53 cued-2BC files carry the same 30 cue timestamps and one of two trial-type sequences. In 24 sessions (every session of 5 of the 9 mPFC mice, Cohort13b M2-1, M2-2, M2-3, M3-2 and M3-3, and 7 cohort-16 sessions) the licks show the forced types swapped, alcohol or sucrose licks only on type-1 trials and water licks only on type-2 trials, against the stored coding (1 forced water, 2 forced alcohol or sucrose); 3 cohort-16 sessions are mixed. The licks do not contradict the choice types (3 and 4), but whether light was delivered on type-4 trials cannot be checked.

The imaging files hold every CNMF-E ROI (1113 in the nonspecific BLA mice against the paper's 540 neurons, 347 against 196 in the BLA-mPFC mice, 748 and 439 against 240 and 281 in the mPFC alcohol sessions). The visual curation the Methods describe is not recorded, so the paper's neurons cannot be selected.

The dandiset holds 37 group-housed male BLA-mPFC neurons from 12 mice; Figure 2c uses 21 from 7. The 2022 cohort holds exactly 21 from 7, but nothing in the files marks the neurons of Figure 2c or Supplementary Table 1.

The BLA imaging files do not say whether GCaMP was expressed in all BLA neurons or only in BLA-mPFC projectors; the virus and experiment description fields are empty in the cued-2BC files. Cohorts 9 and 10 (10 mice) and cohort 16 (11 mice) match the paper's N for the two populations, which is the only basis for telling them apart.

The ranks of the imaged mice are not given (subject descriptions say only cage and mouse number), and 29 nonspecific current clamp neurons from the four 2021 mice carry no rank. The subject name M3.1 is used for two group-housed males recorded on 2024-07-18 (rank 1) and 2024-07-19 (rank 3).

The lick times are stored as the data of TimeSeries that also declare a starting time of 0 and a rate of 100 Hz, so a reader that takes the series at face value gets lick indices, not times. The values are times in seconds on the imaging clock.

Cohort 9 fluorescence traces are nonnegative (minimum exactly 0, up to 7% of samples at 0) and smooth between transients, while the other cohorts' traces take negative values, and the Methods say CNMF-E was run without nonnegativity constraints. On these traces the Methods' z-score against a 3-s baseline is undefined or unbounded for most bouts (62% of bout-neuron pairs have a baseline s.d. under 5% of the session s.d.). Four mPFC sessions hold 44791 to 65535 frames at 10 Hz (75 to 109 min) for 1-h sessions whose last lick is before 3900 s, two of them exactly 65535, the largest 16-bit count.

The alignment of fluorescence and licks could be shown (population response peaking within -2 to 5 s of the bout onsets and above the response at shifted onsets) for 40 of 53 cued-2BC sessions; for the other 13, listed in the imaging notebook's summary, there are few bouts or no peak near lag 0.

Neuron counts per group differ from the paper's in places. Isolated nonspecific neurons 56 from 11 mice (paper 54 from 12), isolated female BLA-mPFC files 14 from 6 (paper 15 from 7), group-housed male BLA-mPFC rank 2 and 3 hold 7 and 17 neurons (paper 9 and 14). The BLA imaging N (10 and 11) includes two mice under the 50-lick exclusion rule of the Methods (44 and 49 alcohol licks).

Questions for the authors. (1) How was the matched number of bouts per condition chosen (Methods, Population-level mean response calculation), at random or the first bouts? The housing comparison of Fig. 5b and the proportions of Fig. 6l,m and Extended Data Fig. 8n reach p < 0.05 here only when the first bouts are taken. (2) Which group-housed male neurons form Figure 2c and Supplementary Table 1? Fig. 2c and the male input resistance pass with all 37 deposited neurons and fail with the 21 of the 2022 cohort. (3) How were five decoding folds per animal formed when most mice have fewer than five water bouts longer than 1 s and 2 s apart? (4) Which BLA imaging cohort is projection-specific? (5) Are the deposited cohort 9 traces the ones analysed, and how were z-scores treated where the 3-s baseline is flat? Cohort 9 is left out of the z-scores here, and the clustering result of Fig. 3f holds only when it is kept with a floor on the baseline s.d. (6) How were spikes counted in Clampfit on plateaus near the threshold? Whether females fire more at most steps at -20 mV (Fig. 2e) depends on it.

It quoted six sentences the outputs did not support (the ephys Summary's "7 mice" and "15 nonspecific neurons", the channels of recorded files in ephys cell 7, "within 5%" for fig3f, the 13 constant-trace ROIs in imaging cell 11, and the README's "not defined"), all corrected. Imaging cell 10 now prints the cohort-13b sessions that lose pairs to the s.d. floor (none has a constant-trace ROI) and, for its point B11, the isolated bouts with a single lick in the 3-s baseline (101 of 1338, 7.5%; M2 isolates bouts from bouts, so the analyses are unchanged). Its point B9 (ROIs as independent units in the fig3f chi-square) follows the criterion and stays. No outcome changed and none is proposed.

entries.title: Social isolation and BLA-mPFC excitability and activity (Patel, Kim et al. 2026)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Patel, Kim et al. (2026) that dandiset 001454 can test, which are the ex vivo current clamp recordings of BLA-mPFC and nonspecific BLA neurons (Figure 2, Extended Data Figs. 2 and 3) and the calcium imaging of BLA and mPFC neurons in the cued two-bottle choice, with and without BLA-mPFC terminal stimulation (Figures 3, 5 and 6). The home-cage drinking, rank, blood alcohol and optogenetic behaviour data are not in the dandiset, and the resident-intruder imaging has no interaction annotation.
